title: The Pipeline Fails Randomly About One Run in Three
intro: Developers have started habitually clicking 're-run' on red builds. Nobody trusts CI anymore. You've been asked to find out what's going on.

steps.prompt: Look at recent runs of the CI workflow on main.
steps.fake_output:
STATUS   TITLE                    BRANCH  ELAPSED
✓        fix: typo                main    3m02s
X        chore: deps              main    2m51s
✓        chore: deps (rerun)      main    3m05s
X        feat: wishlist           main    2m49s
steps.hint: Same commits passing on re-run means the failures aren't about the code change.

steps.prompt: Check the failed step's logs on the most recent failure (run 9877110).
steps.fake_output:
FAIL src/orders.test.js
  ● order expiry › marks order expired after 1s
    Expected: "expired"
    Received: "pending"
    (test took 1.004s on a shared runner)
steps.hint: Look at what the test depends on.

steps.prompt: Search the other recent failures to see if it's always the same test.
steps.fake_output:
FAIL src/orders.test.js
  ● order expiry › marks order expired after 1s
steps.hint: The same test failing intermittently across unrelated commits is the signature of a flaky test.

steps.prompt: Find the test in the code.
steps.hint: Real sleeps and exact timing on shared CI hardware are a classic cause of flakiness.

resolution: One test depended on real wall-clock timing: it slept exactly 1000ms and expected a 1000ms timer to have fired. On a fast laptop that works; on busy shared CI runners, scheduling jitter makes it lose the race about a third of the time. The fix is controlling time instead of waiting for it — fake timers (jest.useFakeTimers / advanceTimersByTime) make the test deterministic and instant. The bigger damage was cultural: once people reflexively re-run red builds, real failures get re-run and merged too. Treat flaky tests as bugs: quarantine them immediately (skip with a linked ticket), fix them quickly, and track flaky-test rates so CI stays trustworthy.
